text:
The European Union formally adopted its twelfth package of sanctions against Russia on Thursday, targeting the shadow fleet of tankers used to circumvent oil price caps and tightening restrictions on dual-use goods exports.

The sanctions package introduces a new category of 'critical infrastructure protection' measures, which would penalise third-country operators found to be facilitating the transport of Russian crude above the G7 price ceiling of $60 per barrel.

The United States and the United Kingdom confirmed they would align their own measures with the EU package, extending the coalition of economies imposing the cap. Treasury officials in Washington said enforcement agencies had identified more than 400 vessels operating in the shadow fleet.

Russia's economy ministry dismissed the package as ineffective, pointing to continued oil revenues and stable domestic fuel prices. However, independent analysts noted that Russian crude has been trading at a discount of more than $20 per barrel below Brent, a figure consistent with sanctions pressure.

Hungary, which had previously blocked or delayed earlier packages, agreed to abstain rather than veto following a compromise on agricultural exemptions for bilateral trade with Ukraine.

Human rights organisations called on the EU to add more individuals to the asset-freeze list, arguing that oligarchs with close Kremlin ties continue to access European financial systems through intermediaries.

metadata.title: EU Adopts Twelfth Sanctions Package Targeting Shadow Fleet
